title: Past Continuous vs Past Simple
grammarTitle: Past Continuous vs Past Simple — Choosing the Right Tense
grammarNote: Past Simple описывает ЗАВЕРШЁННЫЕ действия в прошлом — то, что произошло и закончилось. Past Continuous описывает действия, которые ПРОДОЛЖАЛИСЬ в определённый момент. Главный паттерн: "I was doing X (PC = background) when something happened (PS = event)." PC = the stage/setting. PS = the action that changes everything.

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple
grammarTable.example: The power went out at 11:47 p.m. (= single event, done)

grammarTable.subject: Past Continuous
grammarTable.example: She was studying when the power went out. (= ongoing at that moment)

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple
grammarTable.example: He arrived at the station and ate a sandwich. (= one after another)

grammarTable.subject: Past Continuous
grammarTable.example: He was eating a sandwich when the train arrived. (= background action)

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple
grammarTable.example: She read three chapters. (= completed, we know she finished)

grammarTable.subject: Past Continuous
grammarTable.example: She was reading when the lights went out. (= didn't necessarily finish)

rows.example: "I was studying WHEN the phone rang." (studying = ongoing; rang = sudden)
"The wind was howling. Snow was falling." = the stage is set.
"...when the power went out." = event that disrupts the stage.
"She closed her laptop and went to bed." = sequence of completed actions after the event.
yesterday, last night, in 2020, ago, suddenly, immediately, then, after that, at that moment, once
while, when (+ PS event), at 11 p.m., all evening, throughout, during, as, at that time
"When the alarm rang, she was sleeping." — "when" + PS interrupts the PC action.
"While she was sleeping, the alarm rang." — "while" always introduces the longer PC action.

grammarExtra.title: PS for sequence vs PC for simultaneous

rows.example: "He arrived at the station. He bought a ticket. He got on the train." = one after another.

rows.form: PC simultaneous: while, at the same time
rows.example: "While Kamila was telling stories, Rustam was scaring everyone." = both at once.

rows.form: Test: can you say "at the same time"?
rows.example: If yes → both PC. If one happens AFTER → PS for both (sequence).

rows.form: ✗ "I was studying all night" (if you finished)
rows.example: ✅ "I studied all night." — if it's a completed period, PS is more natural.
✅ "When I arrived, she left." — two sequential events = both PS.

rows.form: ✗ "She was falling asleep when her alarm rang."
rows.example: ✅ "She fell asleep when her alarm rang." OR "She was falling asleep when her alarm rang." — both possible, but PS clearer for completed action.
✅ "I knew she was tired." — stative verb = always Past Simple.

grammarTip:
Простое правило для выбора:
① Это ЗАВЕРШЁННОЕ действие? → Past Simple
② Это было В ПРОЦЕССЕ в момент прошлого? → Past Continuous
③ Два действия: одно ПРЕРЫВАЕТ другое → длинное = PC, короткое = PS
④ Два действия ОДНОВРЕМЕННО → оба PC (while)
⑤ Последовательность действий (одно за другим) → оба PS

💡 Самый надёжный тест: «Можно ли сказать 'в это время шёл процесс'?» → Да = PC. «Просто произошло и закончилось?» → PS.

exercises.text: Kamila ___ when Rustam ___ to the group chat.
exercises.hint: Background: was sleeping (PC). Shorter event: sent a message (PS).

exercises.text: While the students ___ (chat) in the hallway, the power ___ (come) back on.
exercises.hint: "while" + PC (background). PS = the event that changed things: "came back on".

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence that shows a SEQUENCE of completed actions.
exercises.text: Which sentence shows actions one after another?
opts: She was running while he was calling.
She ran, stopped, and called him back.
She was running when he called.
While she was calling, he was waiting.
exercises.correct: She ran, stopped, and called him back.
exercises.hint: Sequence = three completed Past Simple actions one after another: ran → stopped → called.

exercises.text: "He was arriving when she left." is the most natural way to say both actions happened quickly.
exercises.hint: ✅ "He arrived when she left." — two sequential, short events = both Past Simple is more natural.

exercises.instruction: What does the difference in tense show?
exercises.text: "She read three chapters." vs "She was reading a chapter when the lights went out."
opts: "Read" = finished; "was reading" = may not have finished
exercises.correct: "Read" = finished; "was reading" = may not have finished
exercises.hint: PS: she finished the chapters. PC: she was in the middle of reading — the lights went out, so we don't know if she finished.

exercises.text: Amir ___ (type) his conclusion when the power ___ (go out).
exercises.hint: Longer background: was typing (PC). Sudden interruption: went out (PS).

exercises.text: Rustam ___ onto the train, ___ his bag, and ___ into his bunk.
opts: was getting / was putting / was climbing
exercises.hint: Sequence of completed actions = all Past Simple. got → put → climbed (one after another).

opts: While the train arrived, she was reading.
While she was reading, the train arrived.
While she read, the train was arriving.
While the train was arriving, she read.
exercises.correct: While she was reading, the train arrived.
exercises.hint: "While" introduces the longer ongoing PC action. The shorter event (train arrived) is PS.

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: "She ___ her novel when I called."
questions.hint: Background action = PC. Shorter interrupting event (called) = PS. "She was reading when I called." ✅

questions.text: Choose the correct tense: "He ___ , sat down, and opened his book."
questions.hint: Sequence: arrived → sat → opened = all Past Simple. "Arrived, sat, opened" = one after another.
While + PC (longer background). Short event = PS: cut out.

questions.text: "She was studying all night." — When is Past Simple more natural?
opts: When the studying was completed (she finished)
When we don't know if she finished
questions.correct: When the studying was completed (she finished)
questions.hint: "She studied all night." = completed period, she finished. PS is more natural for completed periods.

questions.text: "While I ___ , she ___." Which pair shows simultaneous actions?
questions.hint: Simultaneous ongoing actions = both PC: was studying + was calling. "While" confirms they happened at the same time.
Sequence of two completed actions = both Past Simple: finished → went.

questions.text: "The wind was howling. Snow was falling." What is this called?
questions.hint: Multiple Past Continuous actions setting the atmosphere/background of a story = scene-setting.

questions.text: "She was reading THREE chapters." — What does this suggest?
opts: She may not have finished — action was in progress
questions.correct: She may not have finished — action was in progress
questions.hint: PC = action in progress, possibly unfinished. PS ("she read") = she completed them.

questions.text: "___ I was ___ the essay, Kamila was sleeping." Which word fits?
questions.hint: "While" introduces the ongoing background action (PC). "While I was writing..." ✅

questions.text: Complete: "Suddenly, the lights ___ (go out) while everyone ___ (study)."
"When I arrived, she was leaving" means they were both there at the same moment.
questions.hint: "She was leaving" = in the middle of leaving = still there when he arrived. Their actions overlapped for a moment.

questions.text: "I ___ three times before I finally reached her." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: "Three times" = completed number of times = Past Simple. Counted, completed actions always use PS.
"while" + PC = correct. "while" + PS sequence is unusual — "while" implies simultaneity, not sequence.

questions.text: "As the train ___ (move) through the steppe, Rustam ___ (think) about the future."
questions.hint: "As" = while = both actions simultaneous → both PC: was moving / was thinking.

questions.text: Choose the most natural sentence for a sequence.
opts: While he woke up, while he showered, he ate.
He was waking up, showering, and eating.
He woke up, showered, and ate breakfast.
He was waking up when he showered.
questions.correct: He woke up, showered, and ate breakfast.
questions.hint: Sequence of morning actions = all Past Simple: woke → showered → ate. No PC needed for simple sequences.

questions.text: "I was wanting to help but I didn't know how." — What is wrong?
opts: The tense is wrong — use future
questions.hint: "want" is stative → always Past Simple: "I wanted to help but I didn't know how." ✅
